Done. Solution succeeded on the first run:

- `out/T4/solution.py` — plain torch/safetensors script (both in `F-allowed.md`) that: loads the sharded base and the two flat fine-tune checkpoints, verifies identical key sets and 114/48/66 counts, verifies the 66 non-MLP tensors are bit-identical across all three checkpoints (aborting loudly otherwise), computes each of the 48 MLP tensors as `base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base)` in float32 against the unmodified base, copies the rest from base, and asserts the output has exactly 114 tensors before saving.
- `out/T4/run.sh` — invokes it.
- `out/T4/model.safetensors` — output, verified to contain 114 tensors.
- `out/T4/REPORT.md` — participant self-report.

I chose a plain script over `mergekit`'s task-arithmetic config because the required precondition checks and exact-count asserts are simplest to guarantee directly in code rather than bolted onto a merge tool.
